submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on text about cultivating crops or plants (agronomy/horticulture: fields, soil, fertilizer or pesticide application, irrigation, weeds competing with crops, plants grown under given conditions, harvests, drought, lawns): activation switches on at the first crop/plant-cultivation word and stays high over the following tokens of that clause, usually peaking on the verbs, prepositions, conjunctions and punctuation after the topic word (e.g. 'applied', 'for', 'under', 'during', 'and', '.') rather than on the topic noun itself; one short sentence is enough, no long context is required. It is weak (under about 30% of max) for livestock/animal husbandry and forestry/logging, and near zero for the same sentence frames about non-agricultural subjects (finance, plumbing, cell culture, computers, cooking, code).
